judge_runs.rationale: The candidate tracks point (47) verbatim: "references in this Regulation to the AI Office shall be construed as references to the Commission". The modal "shall" is present in the source, and the action ("construe as references to the Commission") and object ("references in this Regulation to the AI Office") reproduce the wording without broadening or narrowing. The clause is passively framed and names no addressee, so actor "unspecified_needs_review" is the correct handling and no actor has been invented. No scoping clause or carve-out attaches to this sentence, so nothing has been dropped, and Article 3 is operative binding text rather than a recital. Scores for normative relevance and operational utility are reduced because this is an interpretive/deeming rule within a definitions article rather than a conduct-shaping duty on an identifiable party, which makes the classification as an "obligation" defensible but of limited engineering actionability.

Point (48) of Article 3 contains an operative interpretive clause with an explicit modal: 'as regards AI systems put into service or used by Union institutions, agencies, offices and bodies, references to national competent authorities or market surveillance authorities in this Regulation shall be construed as references to the European Data Protection Supervisor.' The candidate's action ('construe as references to the European Data Protection Supervisor'), object ('references to national competent authorities or market surveillance authorities in this Regulation') and the scoping condition ('as regards AI systems put into service or used by Union institutions, agencies, offices and bodies') are all verbatim-grounded, and no further condition or carve-out in the sentence has been dropped. The 'shall'-based deontic classification as an obligation is defensible, although the provision is a deeming/interpretation rule addressed to no particular addressee, so 'unspecified_needs_review' is the correct actor treatment (the text genuinely names no duty-bearer and no Article 16-style inference applies; the actor_inference_source_node_id pointing at the same definitional node is redundant but harmless). The source is binding operative text in Article 3, not a recital, so the binding-source check holds.
